subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should webhook deliveries with the same resolved sessionKey be rejected, queued, or left parallel by default, and should that behavior be opt-in per hook/mapping?
rationale: This changes an external HTTP contract and retry semantics for existing webhook integrations, so automation should not choose the permanent 409 versus queue versus compatibility default policy.

options.title: Opt-in overlap policy
options.body: Add an explicit hook or mapping policy such as skip/queue/parallel while preserving today's default behavior for existing callers.

options.title: Unconditional 409 guard
options.body: Implement the reporter's exact behavior for all same-session active hook deliveries, accepting the compatibility break for callers that currently expect 200/runId.

options.title: Fold into queued ingestion
options.body: Defer the specific guard until the broader webhook queue design decides durable backlog, parallelism, and caller response semantics together.

recommendation.title: Opt-in overlap policy
recommendation.body: Add an explicit hook or mapping policy such as skip/queue/parallel while preserving today's default behavior for existing callers.

likelyOwner.reason: The current hook/cron codepath blame and repository ownership trail make @steipete the best available owner for the compatibility and API-shape decision.
